messages:
jlee: Heads-up — SAST job failed on PR #842. Error looks KMS-related and I can't find corresponding audit log entries for the key access. Anyone seen this pattern?

miriam: Can you paste the CI error? :eyes:

jlee: Sure, from the CI run:```
2026-03-19T21:03:12Z ERROR: KMS Decrypt failed: permissionDenied: serviceAccount:ci-runner@redwood-ci.iam.gserviceaccount.com not authorized
at kmsclient.Decrypt (kms.go:142)
```

aaron-bot: Automated note — CI job 842 failed (sast-scan). Trace: https://ci.redwood.internal/842 — tagging sec queue.

lina: Did infra change RBAC on the keystore last night? I remember a short window where we removed a legacy binding for cleanup. :thinking_face:

miriam: Yep, I ran a terraform apply to remove a stale group binding. I thought it was only for the prod key `projects/redwood/locations/global/keyRings/infra/cryptoKeys/legacy` — maybe I scoped too wide. I didn't touch CI service account intentionally.

jlee: If the SAST runner couldn't decrypt the fixtures, that would cause the scanner to bail out -> missing evidence and the pipeline marks PR as failed. But why no audit log? I expected a KMS audit entry even on denied attempts.

aaron-bot: Quick check: if auth fails before KMS endpoint call (e.g., token exchange fails) you may not see KMS audit entries. Check Cloud Audit Logs for "iam.googleapis.com" token errors and the CI runner credentials logs.

lina: Here's the relevant Logs Explorer query I used: `resource.type="k8s_container" AND protoPayload.methodName:"google.iam.credentials"` — returns a handful of token-exchange errors at 21:02UTC. Link: https://logs.redwood.internal/explorer?q=...

miriam: Ok that matches my apply time. I must have removed a binding that allowed the CI SA to impersonate `ci-runner@redwood-ci`. I'm going to re-add a temporary grant `roles/iam.serviceAccountTokenCreator` scoped just to the CI runner service account.

jlee: Please add an audit comment to the terraform PR and ping infra on the change. We need a postmortem note on why SAST treats missing fixtures as a blocker. Could we instead make the scanner mark missing fixture decrypt as "skipped" so it doesn't block merges? :shrug:

security-squad: We should avoid suppressing too widely — better to fail-to-review than silently pass. Suggestion: add a clearer failure reason and a link to remediation steps in the CI log (so engineers know to ask infra).

oncall_sre: I can coordinate a short rollback window if needed. Propose: re-add the binding now as a hotfix, run one full SAST run, then we create INFRA ticket to refine scoping. ETA 15m.

miriam: Hotfix applied — terraform state updated, re-granting the impersonation binding to `ci-team@redwood` for the CI runner only. I'll push the PR for the narrow-scoped fix and link the plan output.

jlee: Running the CI scan again now. If it passes, we'll follow up with an action item list: 1) INFRA-1942 to audit all key bindings and set an allowlist for CI SAs; 2) SAST-138 to improve scanner behavior for missing decrypted fixtures; 3) SEC-LOGS-21 to add a synthetic check that alerts when key access audit logs go silent for >5m.

aaron-bot: CI job 843 queued. SAST run in progress.

jlee: Scan passed. :tada: No more KMS errors. Miriam — add the PR link and the terraform diff to INFRA-1942 and assign to infra-owners.

miriam: Will do. Also adding a short blameless note in the security postmortem channel with root cause: overly-broad terraform prune removed an impersonation binding.

security-squad: Also recommending we add a docs snippet for engineers: how to read KMS + IAM failures in CI and the minimal fix steps (grant vs. revoke). I'll draft that and post to #docs-devsec.

oncall_sre: Closing handoff — no live incident, just a production-weirdness during infra cleanup. If anyone sees re-occurrence, tag @oncall_sre immediately.

jlee: Thanks all. INFRA-1942 created: https://tickets.redwood.internal/INFRA-1942 — assigning to infra and security for follow-up.
